capability_declaration.evidence: IEC 61850 defines Logical Nodes (LNs) and Data Objects (DOs) that explicitly describe device capabilities, functions, and services. The ACSI (Abstract Communication Service Interface) and SCL (Substation Configuration Language) — particularly ICD (IED Capability Description) and CID files — allow devices/agents to formally declare their capabilities, supported services, and data models (IEC 61850-6, IEC 61850-7-2, IEC 61850-7-4).
capability_declaration.rationale: SCL ICD files and Logical Node definitions provide a structured, machine-readable capability declaration mechanism directly specified in the standard.

bounded_authority.evidence: IEC 61850-8-1 and IEC 61850-7-2 define access control at the service level (e.g., read/write permissions on data attributes, control authority via SBO — Select-Before-Operate — and direct control models). Control blocks (GOOSE, Sampled Values, Reporting) have configurable parameters limiting scope. However, explicit agent-level authority ceilings, time-bound delegation, or revocation mechanisms for autonomous AI agents are not directly specified.
bounded_authority.rationale: SBO control models and access permissions provide partial authority bounding, but time-expiry, delegation chains, and AI-agent-specific revocation are absent.

decision_auditability.evidence: IEC 61850-7-2 specifies logging services (LOG, LOGCTL logical nodes) and reporting mechanisms (BRCB/URCB — Buffered/Unbuffered Report Control Blocks) that record events, state changes, and control actions with timestamps. IEC 61850-7-4 defines the LPHD and LGOS logical nodes for health and status tracking. However, attribution of decisions to a specific autonomous agent, reasoning traceability, or AI-specific audit trail requirements are not addressed.
decision_auditability.rationale: Logging and reporting services cover event/action recording with timestamps, but lack agent attribution and decision-reasoning traceability needed for AI auditability.

data_governance.evidence: IEC 61850 does not contain explicit clauses on data ownership, consent, or retention policies. Some implicit governance can be inferred from access control settings on data attributes (IEC 61850-7-2 ACSI) and the SCL configuration model which defines who can read/write data. Cybersecurity extensions (IEC 62351 series, referenced by IEC 61850) touch on authentication and access, but data governance in the modern sense (GDPR-style ownership, consent, retention schedules) is absent.
data_governance.rationale: No explicit data governance clauses exist; only implicit access control structures allow inference of rudimentary data governance principles.
